top_story.headline: Rep. LaMonica McIver's campaign discloses eight late 48-hour notices and a $2,000 excess contribution after an FEC inquiry
top_story.dek: A Form 99 filed Tuesday blames a platform switch for a string of reporting errors in the committee's July Quarterly Report and its 48-hour notices.
paragraphs: In a Form 99 received October 13, LaMonica McIver for Congress (Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-NJ) answered an FEC request for additional information dated October 8, 2026 about its July Quarterly Report (05/14/2026 to 06/30/2026). The committee says it did not file timely 48-hour notices for eight contributions of $1,000 or more received between 05/14 and 05/29/2026. They total $14,000, the largest being $5,000 from LIUNA PAC on 05/26. All eight were disclosed on Schedule A of the quarterly report, and the committee filed the missing notices on 10/13/2026. These are late disclosures, filed roughly five months after the contributions arrived.

The committee also says four contributions reported on a 05/16 48-hour notice were left off the original Schedule A: $2,500 from Defend the Vote, $2,500 from John Graham, and $1,000 each from Sara McVicker and Bert Speelpenning. A further 235 ActBlue contributions totaling $7,000 were also omitted, none of them $1,000 or more. It blames a batch-import date error after moving from FECFile to the NGP reporting platform. A separate item concerns Joseph W. Kaempfer Jr.: his $5,000 ActBlue contribution on 05/20/2026, combined with an earlier $500, put his primary total $2,000 over the $3,500 limit. The committee says he confirmed in writing that he wants that $2,000 redesignated to the general election instead of refunded, to be reported on the Post-General Report.

The red-flag keyword scan hit one other filing: National Association of Addiction Treatment Providers described a credit card testing fraud incident on its donation platform. The filing shows 167 unauthorized micro-transactions totaling $19.60, which is far smaller than the keywords suggest. Details are in the Form 99 section.

sections.headline: Fourteen RFAIs and one Form 99 for sitting members, mostly excessive contributions and LLC questions
paragraphs: Fifteen filings received October 12-13 involve sitting lawmakers: 14 RFAI letters, each with a response due 11/16 or 11/17/2026, and McIver's Form 99 (summarized in the Top Story). Five come from New Jersey members (Norcross, Smith, Menendez, Pallone, McIver). Three RFAIs went to Hern for Senate, whose treasurer, Paul Kilgore, is also assistant treasurer of Sununu Senator (see Form 99 section). Lisa Lisker is treasurer of both Troy Downing for Congress and Alme for Senate (see RFAI section).

items: Rep. Darren Soto (D-FL), Darren Soto for Congress (treasurer Melissa Nissen), RFAI on the 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (07/01-07/29/2026). Item 1 flags contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits. Item 2 asks the committee to clarify whether LLC donors are taxed as partnerships; the FEC notes the committee's earlier explanation of its corrective action. Filing.

Rep. Donald Norcross (D-NJ), Donald Norcross for Congress (treasurer Melissa D. Pollitt), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report (05/14-06/30/2026). Schedule A shows contributions that appear to come from corporations or labor organizations, which must be refunded within 30 days of the treasurer learning of them. The letter also asks whether LLC donors are treated as partnerships. Filing.

Rep. Christopher H. Smith (R-NJ), Friends of Chris Smith (treasurer Mary Roldan), RFAI on the 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (04/01-05/13/2026). The letter asks about LLC contributions and about contributions from an organization that is not a registered political committee, which must show the money came from a permissible account. Filing.

Rep. Jimmy Patronis (R-FL), Friends of Jimmy Patronis, Inc. (treasurer Zac Funderburk), RFAI on a pre-primary report. Schedule A shows contributions through a conduit without the original earmarked contributions itemized. The FEC's record tags Patronis as a challenger. Filing.

Rep. Jimmy Patronis (R-FL), Friends of Jimmy Patronis, Inc., second RFAI the same day, on the April Quarterly Report (01/01-03/31/2026): contributions that appear to exceed the limits and may have to be refunded, redesignated or reattributed within 60 days. Filing.

Rep. Kevin Hern (R-OK), Hern for Senate (treasurer Paul Kilgore; FEC lists Hern as an S-OK challenger), RFAI on the Amended 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (04/01-05/27/2026, received 09/29/2026). The report discloses activity outside its coverage dates, and the FEC wants it moved to the correct reports. Filing.

Rep. Kevin Hern (R-OK), Hern for Senate, RFAI on the Amended April Quarterly Report (01/01-03/31/2026, received 09/29/2026). The letter says the report should include only activity from 1/1/2026 to 3/31/2026, which appears to be the same out-of-period problem. Filing.

Rep. Kevin Hern (R-OK), Hern for Senate, RFAI on the Amended July Quarterly Report (05/28-06/30/2026, received 09/29/2026). The FEC noted several redesignations or reattributions and asked that they be reported in the required three-memo-entry format (original, negative reversal, new designation). Filing.

Rep. Timothy M. Kennedy (D-NY), Kennedy for Congress (treasurer Lauren Decot Lee), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report (06/04-06/30/2026). The committee filed a 48-hour notice for a 'last minute' contribution from LPL Financial LLLC Political Action Committee on 06/15/2026, but it does not appear on Schedule A. Filing.

Rep. Robert Menendez (D-NJ), Menendez for Congress (treasurer John Palumbo), RFAI on a pre-primary report with three items. Excessive contributions: the FEC notes some corrective action but says at least one apparent excess has not been refunded, redesignated or reattributed within 60 days. LLC contributions, with the same partnership question. Redesignation and reattribution memo entries that need reformatting. Filing.

Rep. Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ), Pallone for Congress (treasurer Peter D. Nichols), RFAI on the April Quarterly Report with three items. Some excessive contributions were refunded, but others were not within 60 days and 'must be refunded immediately.' A disbursement to Round World Consulting with the purpose 'Prior Period Void - Communication Services' could be a prohibited corporate contribution if the services were provided without payment. Contributions from an unregistered organization also need clarification. Filing.

Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott (D-VA), Scott for Congress (treasurer Sean M. Williamson), RFAI on the Amended 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (07/01-07/15/2026, received 10/08/2026). Line 17 disbursements rose $45,914.15 from the original report, and the FEC asks why that spending was not disclosed originally. Filing.

Rep. Thomas R. Suozzi (D-NY), Suozzi for Congress (treasurer Michael G. Norman), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. Transfers from 'Democracy Summer 2026' appear to come through joint fundraising, but that committee is not listed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization. Filing.

Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT), Troy Downing for Congress (treasurer Lisa Lisker), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. Conduit contributions lack the original earmarked contributions. The FEC also says the committee ID listed for Steve Daines For Montana (C90015348) appears to be incorrect. Filing.

Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-NJ), LaMonica McIver for Congress (treasurer Lashea McIver), Form 99 received 10/13/2026 answering the FEC's 10/08 request on the July Quarterly Report. It discloses eight 48-hour notices totaling $14,000 that were not filed on time (late disclosures, filed 10/13), four omitted contributions, and a $2,000 excess from Joseph W. Kaempfer Jr. to be redesignated to the general election. Full detail in the Top Story. Filing.

sections.headline: Thirty-eight more RFAIs: cash-balance mismatches, negative cash, and amended reports with unexplained changes
paragraphs: Thirty-eight RFAIs went to challengers, open-seat and presidential candidates, PACs and party committees. Candidate committees are 23 of them and PACs or party committees 15. Recurring themes are beginning cash balances that do not match prior reports, Column B totals that are wrong, and amended reports whose disbursements, receipts or debts changed. McClainforcongresssc and Dr. Sonia for Congress each received two letters with negative ending cash balances, and Southern States Police Benevolent Assoc PAC Fund received three. One letter, to Tom Willis Victory, reverses an approved termination. Responses are due 11/16 or 11/17/2026.

items: Alme for Senate (candidate committee; Kurt Alme, R-MT, open seat; treasurer Lisa Lisker, who is also treasurer of Troy Downing for Congress), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report with five items. Excessive contributions not yet refunded, redesignated or reattributed within 60 days. Contributions designated for the 2026 primary but received after it, allowed only to the extent of net primary debts. LLC contributions. A fourth item that appears to follow the FEC's standard text on contributions from unregistered organizations. Transfers from 2026 Senators Classic Committee and Senate Path to Victory that appear to be joint fundraising but are not on the Statement of Organization. Filing.

American College of Radiology Association PAC (PAC; treasurer Mary F. Scanlon), RFAI on the August Monthly Report (07/01-07/31/2026). Schedule E shows independent expenditures for Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz in the Florida 20th District primary, but the office-sought information is for the 25th District. Refunds of contributions to candidates were also put on the wrong summary line. Filing.

Anew Day (House candidate committee; treasurer Denia Eisenhower Delgado), RFAI on the Statement of Organization. The principal campaign committee's name does not include the candidate's name, as 11 CFR 102.14(a) requires. Filing.

Bridgford for Iowa (candidate committee; Michael Bridgford, I-IA; treasurer Hans Schneckloth), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report (04/01-06/30/2026) with five items. Excessive contributions. A missing Schedule A for the amount on Line 13(b), loans. In-kind contributions on Schedule B that need itemizing on Schedule A. Possibly unfiled 48-hour notices for 'last minute' contributions after the 12 Day Pre-Primary close of books. Whether a candidate loan came from personal funds or a bank or other line of credit. Filing.

California Young Democrats Fed PAC (party-type committee; treasurer Chris Thomas), RFAI on the Mid-Year Report (04/01-06/30/2026). The beginning cash balance does not equal the April Quarterly ending balance, and the Column B totals on lines 6(c), 11(a)(i), 11(a)(iii), 11(d), 19 and 20 look wrong. Filing.

Case New Holland Industrial Inc. Excellence in Government Fund (PAC; treasurer Matthew Hart), RFAI on the Amended August Monthly Report (07/01-07/31/2026, received 09/18/2026). Disbursements rose $15,000 from the original. The committee's memo text said three July disbursements were erroneously left off the original report. Filing.

Congress Majority PAC (PAC; treasurer Max E. Coston), RFAI on the September Monthly Report (08/01-08/31/2026). Schedule B shows a refund of a contribution to Nicholas Bini, but the original contribution does not appear to have been reported. Filing.

Democrats Who Win (PAC; treasurer Brian Foucart), RFAI on the October Monthly Report (09/01-09/30/2026). Transfers to affiliated committees were reported on the wrong summary line and belong on a Schedule B supporting Line 22. Filing.

Dr. Sonia for Congress (candidate committee; Sonia Devgan-Kacker, D-CA, open seat; treasurer James T. Perez), RFAI on the Amended 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (received 07/09/2026). The beginning cash balance does not match the April Quarterly ending balance, and the report shows negative ending cash of $15,106.32, which could be a debt, an error or a prohibited bank overdraft. Filing.

Dr. Sonia for Congress, second RFAI the same day, on the Amended July Quarterly Report (05/14-06/30/2026, received 08/04/2026). The beginning cash again does not match the prior report, 48-hour notices for 'last minute' contributions may be missing, and ending cash is negative $16,662.65. Filing.

Eisenhauer for Congress (candidate committee; Michael D. Eisenhauer, I-MT; treasurer Katie Dasinger), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report with four items. Contributions designated for the primary but received after it. Incorrect Column B totals on many lines. A beginning cash balance that does not match the 12 Day Pre-Primary ending balance. Schedule C no longer shows whether a candidate loan came from personal funds. Filing.

Eric Yonce for US House of Representatives (candidate committee; Eric Yonce, D-FL, who is also the treasurer), RFAI on a pre-primary report received 09/16/2026. Column B totals look wrong on about 20 lines, the beginning cash does not match the July Quarterly ending balance, and earmarked contributions lack required conduit information. Filing.

Everett W. Wess for US Senate (candidate committee; Everett W. Wess, D-AL, open seat, who is also the treasurer), RFAI on the Amended 12 Day Pre-Run-Off Report (04/30-05/27/2026, received 09/11/2026). Line 17 disbursements fell $32,175.00 from the original report, and the FEC asks for an explanation. Filing.

Fight for Working People (PAC; treasurer Jef Green), RFAI on a 48-Hour Notification Report received 09/18/2026. The independent expenditure report lacks required itemized details, and the FEC asks for a complete amended report including the calendar-year-to-date and per-election totals. Filing.

GETMO (presidential candidate committee; Ryan Jackson, Libertarian, who is also the treasurer), RFAI on the Statement of Organization. The letter cites the same committee-naming rule, 11 CFR 102.14(a), as the Anew Day letter, and the committee's name does not contain the candidate's name. Filing.

Hach for Congress (candidate committee; Gregory Hach, R-NY; treasurer Nancy H. Watkins), RFAI on the April Quarterly Report (received 06/10/2026). Excessive contributions. The FEC notes the committee's corrective action but says some excess contributions have not been refunded, redesignated or reattributed. Filing.

Indivisible Action (PAC; treasurer Elizabeth Ramey), RFAI on the September Monthly Report. Dates of disbursement on 24- and 48-hour independent expenditure reports naming 'Good Influence,' 'Scale to Win' and 'Taskforce' as payees do not match Schedule E entries. Filing.

Jackie Auringer for Congress (candidate committee; Jackie Mary Auringer, R-NY; treasurer Bruce R. McLean), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. Earmarked contributions through a conduit are not properly itemized, and conduit memo entries were placed on the wrong summary line. Filing.

Lasher for Congress (candidate committee; Micah Charles Lasher, D-NY, open seat; treasurer Robert M. Gottheim), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. 48-hour notices for 'last minute' contributions may be missing, and disbursements described only as 'Political Consulting Fee' need a clearer purpose. Filing.

Maintaining All Republicans in Office PAC (PAC; treasurer Rosemary Canals), RFAI on the Year-End 2025 Report (10/01-12/31/2025). Schedule B shows contributions to candidates that appear to exceed the $5,000-per-election limit for a multicandidate committee. Filing.

McClainforcongresssc (candidate committee; Courtney McClain, D-SC, who is also the treasurer), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report with five items: wrong Column B totals, a beginning cash mismatch, $14,277.06 in unitemized individual receipts, $17,351.97 in operating expenditures with no Schedule B, and negative ending cash of $3,074.91. Filing.

McClainforcongresssc, second RFAI the same day, on the April Quarterly Report. The beginning cash does not match the Amended 2025 Year-End Report received 10/8/2026. The report also shows $17,509.53 in unitemized receipts, $20,040.45 in operating expenditures and negative ending cash of $2,530.92, a repeat of the other letter's problems. Filing.

Melissa Conyears-Ervin for Congress (candidate committee; Melissa Conyears-Ervin, D-IL, open seat; treasurer Jason Ervin), RFAI on the April Quarterly Report (02/26-03/31/2026). Excessive contributions. The letter also says the candidate will not take part in the general election, so general election contributions must be refunded or redesignated to the primary, and they do not appear to have been remedied. Filing.

Mullock for Congress (candidate committee; Zack Mullock, D-NJ; treasurer Adam Erickson), RFAI on a pre-primary report. Column B totals on lines 7(a), 7(c), 13(a), 13(c), 16, 17 and 22 appear to be incorrect. Filing.

Orange County Republican Executive Committee (party committee; treasurer Wade Bailey), RFAI on the Amended July Quarterly Report (04/01-06/30/2026, received 09/20/2026). The Schedule H2 ratio for 'Lincoln Day 2026 (05/22/2026)' is marked 'new' although it matches the April Quarterly. Payments to Amazon, Family Church, Harbor Freight and Minuteman Press were labeled administrative but described as 'Fundraising Supplies,' 'Room Rental' and 'Event Expense,' which must be allocated under the funds-received method. Filing.

Parrott for Congress (candidate committee; Neil Conrad Parrott, R-MD; treasurer April Parrott), RFAI on the Amended 12 Day Pre-General Report (10/01-10/16/2024, received 07/01/2026). Line 17 disbursements rose $196,131.12 from the original 2024 report. The amendment was received about 20 months after the period it covers. Filing.

Plumbers & Pipefitters Local Union No. 295 PAC (PAC; treasurer Brett Mirsky), RFAI on the October Quarterly Report (07/01-09/30/2026). Receipts labeled 'MEMBER, CONTRIBUTIONS CHECK OFF' were not itemized, and the FEC asks whether any individual aggregates over $200 in the calendar year. Filing.

Scott Wiener for Congress (candidate committee; Scott Wiener, D-CA, open seat; treasurer Stacy Owens), RFAI on the Amended July Quarterly Report (received 09/04/2026). Debts owed to vendors on Line 10 rose $84,369.62 from the original report. Filing.

Southeast Cotton Committee (SECC) Southern Cottongrowers Inc/SE Cotton Ginners Assn (PAC; treasurer Dusty Findley), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. Schedule A shows contributions that appear to exceed the $5,000-per-calendar-year limit. Filing.

Southern States Police Benevolent Assoc PAC Fund (PAC; treasurer Diana Renee Dixon), first of three RFAIs the same day, on the August Monthly Report. The beginning cash does not equal the ending balance of the Amended July Monthly Report received 8/28/26, and Column B totals on lines 7, 29, 31 and 32 appear to be wrong. Filing.
Southern States Police Benevolent Assoc PAC Fund, RFAI on the Amended July Monthly Report (06/01-06/30/2026, received 08/28/2026). Disbursements rose $23,678.89 from the original report. Filing.

Southern States Police Benevolent Assoc PAC Fund, RFAI on the September Monthly Report. The beginning cash does not equal the August Monthly ending balance, and a second item appears to repeat the Column B problem. This is the third letter in a row to the same committee on the same day, so the pattern is serial compliance problems. Filing.

Teamsters Joint Council 53 Political Action Committee (PAC; treasurer Howard Wells), RFAI on the October Quarterly Report. Individual contributors' employer and occupation entries such as 'Local #107 / BA' and 'Local 463 / BA' are not acceptable, and the committee must supply the information or show 'best efforts.' Filing.

Tom Willis Victory (candidate committee; Thomas Edward Willis II, R-WV; treasurer Greg Fornshell), FEC letter dated October 13 changing the committee's status back to quarterly filer. An 08/14/2026 letter had accepted a termination received 07/10/2026. Form 99s filed 09/30 and 10/02 then said candidate loans were not forgiven, the termination request was inadvertent, and the committee wanted to stay active. The committee must now file all required reports. Filing.

Toth for Congress (candidate committee; Steve Toth, R-TX; treasurer Chris Marston), RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. Excessive contributions, some of which the letter says have not been refunded, redesignated or reattributed. Filing.

Turn Left PAC (PAC; treasurer Steven Hall), RFAI on a July Quarterly Report received 09/15/2026. Required 24-Hour reports for 'last minute' independent expenditures may not have been filed. A 24-Hour Report for an expenditure supporting Britta Aguirre was not itemized on Schedule E. Filing.

Valor America (PAC; treasurer Elsy Korah), RFAI on the Amended July Quarterly Report (received 08/09/2026). Receipts rose $24,175 from the original. The committee's memo said the amendment changed total debts, added a debt, and reported an in-kind contribution from a vendor to clear the PAC's debt. Filing.

Williams for Council District 8 in 2028 (listed as a House candidate committee; treasurer Deiontae Davidson), RFAI on the Statement of Organization. The FEC says the Form 1 may have been filed by mistake, since only candidates for U.S. House, Senate or President register with the FEC. A second item follows the same template as the Anew Day letter. Filing.

sections.headline: Thirty-four Form 99s: RFAI responses, below-threshold notices, loan forgiveness, and a $19.60 fraud disclosure
paragraphs: Most of the 34 Form 99s are routine: committees answering FEC letters, or telling the FEC they are below the $5,000 threshold that triggers regular reporting ahead of the October 15 quarterly deadline. Several have no message text in the extracted PDF, and those are described from the filing record. The notable items are the red-flag keyword hit (a small card-testing fraud), Progressive Unity Fund admitting late 24-hour reports, and a $12,750 payment to the same consultant disclosed by California Democratic Party in two months.

items: National Association of Addiction Treatment Providers (PAC, Yakima, WA), red-flag keywords 'fraud' and 'scheme.' The committee reports that on October 8, 2026 it found an automated card-testing scheme on its online donation platform: 167 unauthorized micro-transactions totaling $19.60 from unknown individuals, which it says are not legitimate contributions. It notified the FEC and its bank and worked with its merchant vendor on security fixes. The keyword hit points to an outside attack on the committee's platform, not misconduct by the committee. Filing.

Antoine Kelley for Congress (candidate committee; Antoine F. Kelley Jr., I-GA) says it has not exceeded the statutory threshold and is not required to file the October 15, 2026 Quarterly Report. Filing.
Brandon Griffin for US Senate (candidate committee; Brandon James Griffin, MA) says only 'Committee under $5000.00 threshold.' Filing.

California Democratic Party (state party; treasurer Teddy Kapur) answers a July Monthly Report (06/01-06/30/2026) inquiry. A dialer (non-connected calls) payment did not identify candidates, so it will be amended as an administrative cost on Line 21(b). The party says the administrative payment the FEC asked about is rent, which it left off its April-June reports because it owns its building. A $12,750 non-federal share of a 6/3/26 payment for strategic consulting went to Yvette Martinez, who is not an employee. 401k payments were for employees under 25% federal election activity, and the report was amended. Filing.

California Democratic Party, second Form 99, answers a June Monthly Report (05/01-05/31/2026) inquiry. Descriptions 'mail vol.procesd CA27WhitesidesPri' and 'mail vol.procesd CA32ShermanPri' were amended on 10/13/26 to 'mail volunteer processed CA27 George Whitesides, Primary' and 'mail volunteer processed CA32 Brad Sherman Primary.' A $12,750 non-federal share of a payment made 5/1/26 for strategic consulting went to Yvette Martinez, the same amount and payee as the 6/3/26 payment in the other letter. 401k payments were again described as for employees under 25% federal election activity. Filing.

Carey Baker for Congress (candidate committee; Carey Baker, R-FL, open seat) filed a loan-forgiveness letter dated October 10, 2026. Baker says that effective August 31, 2026 he irrevocably forgives the entire $12,000.00 balance of the personal-funds loan he made to the committee on June 9, 2026, reported under Schedule C transaction ID SC/10.4688. Filing.

CHC BOLD PAC (PAC; treasurer Cassandra Tinsmon) responds to an FEC request on incorrect year-to-date per-election totals in the AZ-01 2026 primary on Schedule E. It blames a software error, says each independent expenditure was reported on time, and says it amended the August and September Monthly Reports. The response is dated on the 10/13/26 due date. Filing.

Citizens for Jamie Hill (candidate committee; Jamie Hill, D-MI) says it filed amended reports because a corrupted FECfile file required recreating the year-end 2025 report, on FEC tech support direction, which changed starting cash on later reports. Filing.

Committee to Elect Lauren Jewett for Congress (candidate committee; Lauren Jewett, D-LA; treasurer Erin Riecke Rowan). The legible text covers in-kind contributions. Louisiana records show some contributors, including The Glitter Bar, are LLCs. The committee asked for IRS Form W-9s and followed up by phone but got no response. It reimbursed the value of two in-kind contributions confirmed to come from prohibited corporate sources, and is still seeking clarification on three LLC contributions. The first page contains no message text. Filing.
E. No-Trump Hansen (Senate candidate committee; E. No-Trump Hansen, D-DE) filed a Form 99 whose extracted PDF contains only the committee header and no message text. Filing.
Friends of Barak Zilberberg (presidential candidate committee; Barak Zilberberg, NPA, Las Vegas) states '0 contributions 0 expenses.' Filing.
Giralt for Wyoming (candidate committee; David Giralt, R-WY, open seat) filed a Form 99 whose extracted PDF contains only the committee header and no message text. Filing.

Hector Mujica for Congress (candidate committee; Hector Daniel Mujica, D-FL; treasurer Jay Petterson). Only the end of the letter is legible. It argues that a rule against accepting transfers that could pay a debt does not apply because the transferred funds were designated for a separate election and could not be used for the outstanding debt, citing 55 Fed. Reg. 26,378 (June 27, 1990). Filing.

Helms/Mobley 2028 - A New Hope (presidential candidate committee; Ron Chad Helms, I) says it has not received contributions or made expenditures over $5,000 from inception through September 30, 2026. Filing.

Hope for Tomorrow - Alan Bond for Congress (candidate committee; Alan Bond, I-NJ), received 10/12, says it has not passed the $5,000 threshold. It reports third-quarter donations of $0 and expenses of $221.97. For February 17 through September 30 it reports donations of $3,795.71, expenses of $3,091.11 and cash on hand of $1,045.54. Filing.
Indigo PAC (PAC, Palo Alto, CA), received 10/12 as a loan-forgiveness filing. John McCrea says that on 09/30/2026 he forgave all debts and loans the PAC owed him, totaling $855.23. Filing.
James Odom Committee (presidential candidate committee; James Odom, R, Austin, TX) says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold and will begin quarterly reports once it does. Filing.

Jillian Gilchrest for Congress (candidate committee; Jillian Gilchrest, D-CT) says it filed a termination report on 10/13/2026 showing cash on hand of negative $51 (the PDF text reads '-$51.00.00'). It says the bank account is actually at $0.00 with no remaining obligations, and asks the FEC to allow the termination despite the discrepancy. Filing.
Kathy McKinstry Campaign (candidate committee; Kathy McKinstry, write-in, OH) says it has not raised or spent more than $5,000. Filing.

Leadership in Action (PAC, Helena, MT; treasurer Katie Wenetta) answers a July Quarterly Report (04/01-06/30/2026) letter about a contribution that did not aggregate correctly. It explains that an Interactive Brokers net gain on investment was negative on the April report and positive on the July report, so the aggregate is the sum of the two. Filing.

Michigan Republican Party (state party) responds to the FEC's September 8, 2026 letter on missing donor identification information for the July Monthly Report (06/01-06/30/2026). It says the clarification is in an amended report filed at the same time. Filing.
People's Courage PAC (PAC; treasurer Judith Zamore) discloses that Olivia Troye LLC, previously Resolute Tenacity LLC, is a single-member LLC wholly owned by Olivia Troye. Filing.

Progressive Unity Fund (PAC; treasurer Peter Frank) answers a September 22, 2026 notice on its July Monthly Report. It acknowledges that 24-Hour reports for some June independent expenditures were not filed on time. It says it filed them June 16, 2026, days after the expenditures and outside the 24-hour window. These are late disclosures. The committee says the expenditures were later fully itemized on Schedule E of the July Monthly Report filed July 20, and calls the delay inadvertent. Filing.
Republican Party of Arkansas (state party) filed a Form 99 whose extracted PDF contains only the committee header and no message text. Filing.
Republican Party of Arkansas, second Form 99 received the same day, which the input identifies as the same document as the first apart from numbers and image IDs. Filing.
Shellyarnoldi4virginia (House candidate committee) says 'I have not raised or spent more than $5,000.' Filing.
Steven Jacob for Kansas 1 (candidate committee; Steven Robert Jacob, Libertarian, KS) says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Filing.

Sununu Senator (candidate committee; John E. Sununu, R-NH, open seat) responds to the FEC's letter on its 12 Day Pre-Primary Report (07/01-08/19/2026). It says the discrepancy in conduit contributions not disclosed in the original earmark is due to unitemized earmarked transactions and chargebacks. The response is signed by assistant treasurer Paul Kilgore, who is also treasurer of Hern for Senate. Filing.
Suzanne Holst (presidential candidate committee, Glendale, CA) says she started the campaign, decided not to move forward, and wants to terminate it, with no funds raised or spent. Filing.
TFM (PAC, Detroit) filed a Form 99 whose extracted PDF contains only the committee header and no message text. Filing.

The Wisco Project PAC (PAC, Shorewood, WI) says it amended its 9/16/26 48-hour notice of independent expenditures, adding $218.15 for rush shipping to the amount paid to Clash Graphics for stickers supporting Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin's 3rd District. The new total is $625.14. Filing.
The Wisco Project PAC, second Form 99 received the same day, which the input identifies as the same document as the first apart from numbers and image IDs. Filing.
